| `lemline.messaging.kafka.<channel>.consumer.offset-reset` |String |`earliest` |`earliest` or `latest` |

Lifecycle events go to a single shared topic:

| Property |Type |Default |Description |
----------------------------------------
| `lemline.messaging.kafka.lifecycleevents.topic` |String |`lemline-lifecycle-events` |Lifecycle events topic |
| `lemline.messaging.kafka.lifecycleevents.producer.topic-out` |String |- |Override of the topic the producer writes to |
| `lemline.messaging.kafka.lifecycleevents.consumer.topic-dlq` |String |`<topic>.dlq` |Dead-letter topic of the lifecycle consumer |

Failed records of the other channels go to `<source-topic>.dlq`.

### RabbitMQ

| Property |Type |Default |Description |
----------------------------------------
| `lemline.messaging.rabbitmq.hostname` |String |`localhost` |Broker host |
| `lemline.messaging.rabbitmq.port` |Integer |`5672` |Broker port |
| `lemline.messaging.rabbitmq.username` |String |`guest` |Username |
| `lemline.messaging.rabbitmq.password` |String |`guest` |Password |
| `lemline.messaging.rabbitmq.virtual-host` |String |`/` |Virtual host |
| `lemline.messaging.rabbitmq.ssl-enabled` |Boolean |- |Connect with TLS |

For each `<channel>` (`commands`, `events`, `cloudevents`, `lifecycleevents`):

| Property |Type |Default |Description |
----------------------------------------
| `lemline.messaging.rabbitmq.<channel>.consumer.concurrency` |Integer |`64` |Consumer concurrency |
| `lemline.messaging.rabbitmq.<channel>.consumer.queue-dlq` |String |- |Dead-letter queue override |
| `lemline.messaging.rabbitmq.<channel>.queue` |String |derived |Queue name override (`commands`, `events`, `cloudevents`). By default the name is derived from the namespaces the runner serves. |

Lifecycle events:

| Property |Type |Default |Description |
----------------------------------------
| `lemline.messaging.rabbitmq.lifecycleevents.queue` |String |`lemline-lifecycle-events` |Lifecycle events queue |
| `lemline.messaging.rabbitmq.lifecycleevents.producer.queue-out` |String |- |Override of the queue the producer writes to |
| `lemline.messaging.rabbitmq.lifecycleevents.producer.exchange-name` |String |- |Override of the exchange the producer writes to |

### PGMQ (PostgreSQL Message Queue)

| Property |Type |Default |
---------------------------
| `lemline.messaging.pgmq.host` |String |`localhost` |
| `lemline.messaging.pgmq.port` |Integer |`5432` |
| `lemline.messaging.pgmq.database` |String |`lemline` |
| `lemline.messaging.pgmq.username` |String |`postgres` |
| `lemline.messaging.pgmq.password` |String |`postgres` |

For each `<channel>` (`commands`, `events`, `cloudevents`, `lifecycleevents`):

| Property |Type |Default |Description |
----------------------------------------
| `lemline.messaging.pgmq.<channel>.consumer.concurrency` |Integer |`64` |Consumer concurrency |
| `lemline.messaging.pgmq.<channel>.consumer.visibility-timeout` |Integer |`30` |Seconds a read message stays invisible to other consumers |
| `lemline.messaging.pgmq.<channel>.consumer.poll-interval` |Integer |`100` |Milliseconds between polls when the queue is empty |
| `lemline.messaging.pgmq.<channel>.consumer.batch-size` |Integer |`10` |Messages read per poll |
| `lemline.messaging.pgmq.<channel>.consumer.max-retries` |Integer |`3` |Deliveries before a message goes to the dead-letter queue |

Lifecycle events:

| Property |Type |Default |Description |
----------------------------------------
| `lemline.messaging.pgmq.lifecycleevents.queue` |String |`lemline-lifecycle-events` |Lifecycle events queue |
| `lemline.messaging.pgmq.lifecycleevents.producer.queue-out` |String |- |Override of the queue the producer writes to |
| `lemline.messaging.pgmq.lifecycleevents.consumer.queue-dlq` |String |- |Dead-letter queue of the lifecycle consumer |

### SQLite

A durable queue stored in one local file, for runners on a single host. Used only when `lemline.messaging.type` is `sqlite`.

| Property |Type |Default |Description |
----------------------------------------
| `lemline.messaging.sqlite.path` |String |`messaging.db` |Queue file. A relative path is resolved against the working directory of the process. Its parent directory must exist. |
| `lemline.messaging.sqlite.visibility-timeout` |Integer |`30` |Seconds a consumer may hold a message before it is delivered again. Set it above the longest time a workflow step can take. |
| `lemline.messaging.sqlite.poll-interval` |Integer |`50` |Milliseconds between polls when the queue is empty |
| `lemline.messaging.sqlite.batch-size` |Integer |`10` |Messages read per poll |
| `lemline.messaging.sqlite.max-retries` |Integer |`3` |Deliveries before a message goes to the dead-letter queue |

These settings apply to every channel.

## Orchestrator

| Property |Type |Default |Description |
----------------------------------------
| `lemline.orchestrator.mode` |String |`action` |`action` sends a message only for tasks that do something (call, run, emit, ...); `all` sends a message for every task, which is mainly useful for end-to-end tests |

## Definitions

| Property |Type |Default |Description |
----------------------------------------
| `lemline.definitions.cache.sync-every` |Duration |`10s` |How often each runner refreshes its cache of workflow definitions from the database |

## Background Tasks (Outboxes and Cleanup)

Runners process durable operations stored in the database (waits, retries, schedules, listeners, gateway starts) and delete old rows.

| Property |Type |Default |Description |
----------------------------------------
| `lemline.scheduled.enabled` |Boolean |`true` |Run background tasks at all. Set by the command line. |

For each `<outbox>` in `wait`, `retry`, `schedule`, `listener`, `gateway`:

| Property |Type |Default |Description |
----------------------------------------
| `lemline.outbox.<outbox>.enabled` |Boolean |`true` |Run this processor |
| `lemline.outbox.<outbox>.outbox.every` |Duration |`10s` |Processing interval |
| `lemline.outbox.<outbox>.outbox.batch-size` |Integer |`1000` |Rows processed per run |
| `lemline.outbox.<outbox>.outbox.initial-jitter` |Duration |`3s` |Maximum random delay before the first run, to spread runners apart |
| `lemline.outbox.<outbox>.outbox.retry-delay` |Duration |`30s` |Base delay before retrying a failed row; doubles on each attempt, with ±20% jitter |
| `lemline.outbox.<outbox>.outbox.max-attempts` |Integer |`5` |Attempts before a row is given up |
| `lemline.outbox.<outbox>.cleanup.every` |Duration |`1h` |Cleanup interval |
| `lemline.outbox.<outbox>.cleanup.initial-jitter` |Duration |`3s` |Maximum random delay before the first cleanup |
| `lemline.outbox.<outbox>.cleanup.after` |Duration |`7d` |Age after which processed rows are deleted |
| `lemline.outbox.<outbox>.cleanup.batch-size` |Integer |`1000` |Rows deleted per run |

`parent` and `fork` only have the `enabled` and `cleanup.*` properties.

Durations accept values such as `500ms`, `10s`, `5m`, `1h` and `7d`.

## Metrics and Health

| Property |Type |Default |Description |
----------------------------------------
| `lemline.metrics.port` |Integer |`8080` |HTTP port of the metrics and health endpoints. `listen --metrics-port` and `gateway start --metrics-port` override it. |
| `lemline.metrics.path` |String |`/q/metrics` |Path of the Prometheus metrics endpoint |

Health checks are served on the same port at `/q/health`, `/q/health/live` and `/q/health/ready`.

## Analytics

| Property |Type |Default |Description |
----------------------------------------
| `lemline.analytics.type` |String |`h2` |`postgresql`, explicit `sqlite`, or `h2` for Lemline's test suite |
| `lemline.analytics.sqlite.path` |String |`analytics.db` |SQLite analytics file. Relative paths use the process working directory. |
| `lemline.analytics.migrate-at-start` |Boolean |`true` |Apply analytics migrations at startup |
| `lemline.analytics.baseline-on-migrate` |Boolean |`false` |Baseline an existing PostgreSQL analytics schema |
| `lemline.analytics.postgresql.host` |String |`localhost` |  |
| `lemline.analytics.postgresql.port` |Integer |`5432` |  |
| `lemline.analytics.postgresql.database` |String |`lemline` |  |
| `lemline.analytics.postgresql.username` |String |`postgres` |  |
| `lemline.analytics.postgresql.password` |String |`postgres` |  |
| `lemline.analytics.postgresql.schema` |String |`lemline` |  |

See [Lifecycle Analytics Reference](lemline-ref-analytics.html).

## Gateway

| Property |Type |Default |Description |
----------------------------------------
| `lemline.gateway.enabled` |Boolean |`false` |Start the gRPC gateway. Set by `lemline gateway start`. |
| `lemline.gateway.grpc.host` |String |`0.0.0.0` |Bind host |
| `lemline.gateway.grpc.port` |Integer |`9000` |Bind port. `gateway start --grpc-port` overrides it. |
| `lemline.gateway.tls.enabled` |Boolean |`true` |Serve gRPC over TLS |
| `lemline.gateway.tls.certificate` |String |- |Server certificate path (required when TLS is enabled) |
| `lemline.gateway.tls.private-key` |String |- |Server private key path (required when TLS is enabled) |
| `lemline.gateway.tls.client-auth` |String |`none` |Client certificate mode: `none`, `request` or `required` |
| `lemline.gateway.tls.trust-store` |String |- |Trust store for client certificates |
| `lemline.gateway.tls.trust-store-password` |String |- |Trust store password |
| `lemline.gateway.authentication.enabled` |Boolean |`true` |Require a JWT bearer token (requires TLS) |
| `lemline.gateway.authentication.jwt.issuer` |String |- |Expected token issuer |
| `lemline.gateway.authentication.jwt.jwks-url` |String |- |JWKS URL used to verify tokens |
| `lemline.gateway.authentication.claims.scope-field` |String |`scope` |Claim holding the scopes |
| `lemline.gateway.authentication.claims.namespaces-field` |String |`lemline_namespaces` |Claim holding the allowed namespaces |
| `lemline.gateway.cors.enabled` |Boolean |`true` |Enable CORS for browser clients |
| `lemline.gateway.cors.origins` |String |`http://localhost:5173` |Allowed origins |
| `lemline.gateway.cors.methods` |String |`GET,POST,OPTIONS` |Allowed methods |
| `lemline.gateway.cors.headers` |String |`Accept,Authorization,Content-Type,Grpc-Timeout,X-Grpc-Web,X-User-Agent` |Allowed request headers |
| `lemline.gateway.watch.poll-interval-ms` |Integer |`250` |Polling interval of watch streams, in milliseconds |
| `lemline.gateway.watch.batch-size` |Integer |`256` |Rows read per watch poll |

See [gRPC Gateway Reference](lemline-ref-gateway.html).

## Security Configuration

There are no `lemline.security.*` settings. Workflow secrets are read from environment variables named after each secret; see [Secrets Reference](lemline-ref-secrets.html).

## Script Runtimes

`run.script` tasks call local executables. Set them with the `lemline.python.exec` and `lemline.node.exec` system properties, or with the `LEMLINE_PYTHON_EXEC` and `LEMLINE_NODE_EXEC` environment variables. They are not read from the configuration file. Defaults: `python3` and `node`.

## Logging

Logging uses the standard Quarkus properties. They are not read from the Lemline configuration file, which only accepts `lemline.*` settings: set them as environment variables or `-D` system properties, for example:

```BASH
export QUARKUS_LOG_LEVEL=INFO
export QUARKUS_LOG_CONSOLE_LEVEL=DEBUG   # the console only shows ERROR by default
export QUARKUS_LOG_CATEGORY__COM_LEMLINE__LEVEL=DEBUG
```

From the command line, `--debug`, `--info`, `--warn` and `--error` set the log level, and `--json` switches to JSON logs. The default level is `ERROR`.

## Example

```YAML
lemline:
  database:
    type: postgresql
    migrate-at-start: true
    postgresql:
      host: db.internal
      database: lemline
      username: lemline
  messaging:
    type: kafka
    kafka:
      brokers: kafka-1:9092,kafka-2:9092
      commands:
        consumer:
          concurrency: 32
```

Keep passwords out of the file: set them with environment variables such as `LEMLINE_DATABASE_POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD`.

# Environment Variables Reference

This reference lists the environment variables the Lemline runner reads.

## Configuration Properties as Environment Variables

Every property of the [Runner Configuration Reference](lemline-ref-config.html) can be set with an environment variable. The variable name is the property name in upper case, with every character that is not a letter or a digit replaced by `_`:

| Property |Environment variable |
----------------------------------
| `lemline.database.type` |`LEMLINE_DATABASE_TYPE` |
| `lemline.database.postgresql.password` |`LEMLINE_DATABASE_POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD` |
| `lemline.messaging.kafka.brokers` |`LEMLINE_MESSAGING_KAFKA_BROKERS` |
| `lemline.messaging.kafka.commands.consumer.group-id` |`LEMLINE_MESSAGING_KAFKA_COMMANDS_CONSUMER_GROUP_ID` |
| `lemline.gateway.authentication.jwt.jwks-url` |`LEMLINE_GATEWAY_AUTHENTICATION_JWT_JWKS_URL` |

Environment variables override the configuration file and are overridden by Java system properties (`-D...`).

The same rule applies to Quarkus properties, for example `QUARKUS_LOG_LEVEL` for `quarkus.log.level`.

## Variables Read Directly by Lemline

| Environment Variable |Default |Description |
----------------------------------------------
| `LEMLINE_CONFIG` |- |Path of the configuration file, used when `--config` is not given. The file must exist. |
| `LEMLINE_PYTHON_EXEC` |`python3` |Python executable used by `run.script` tasks with `language: python` (also settable with the `lemline.python.exec` system property) |
| `LEMLINE_NODE_EXEC` |`node` |Node.js executable used by `run.script` tasks with `language: js` (also settable with the `lemline.node.exec` system property) |

## Secrets Environment Variables

Workflow secrets are read from environment variables named exactly like the secrets the workflow declares in `use.secrets`: no prefix and no name conversion.

| Declared secret |Environment variable read by the runner |
------------------------------------------------------------
| `PAYMENT_API_KEY` |`PAYMENT_API_KEY` |
| `DB_CREDENTIALS` |`DB_CREDENTIALS` (a JSON object value is parsed) |

See [Secrets Reference](lemline-ref-secrets.html).

## Commonly Used Quarkus Variables

| Environment Variable |Default |Description |
----------------------------------------------
| `QUARKUS_LOG_LEVEL` |`ERROR` |Root log level. The `--debug`, `--info`, `--warn` and `--error` options set it too. |
| `QUARKUS_LOG_CONSOLE_JSON_ENABLED` |`false` |JSON console logs. The `--json` option sets it too. |

## Environment Variable Usage Example

```BASH
# Database configuration
export LEMLINE_DATABASE_TYPE="postgresql"
export LEMLINE_DATABASE_POSTGRESQL_HOST="postgres.example.com"
export LEMLINE_DATABASE_POSTGRESQL_DATABASE="lemline_prod"
export LEMLINE_DATABASE_POSTGRESQL_USERNAME="lemline_user"
export LEMLINE_DATABASE_POSTGRESQL_PASSWORD="secret-password"

# Messaging configuration
export LEMLINE_MESSAGING_TYPE="kafka"
export LEMLINE_MESSAGING_KAFKA_BROKERS="kafka-1:9092,kafka-2:9092"
export LEMLINE_MESSAGING_KAFKA_COMMANDS_CONSUMER_GROUP_ID="lemline-prod"

# Logging configuration
export QUARKUS_LOG_LEVEL="INFO"

# Workflow secrets (named exactly like the entries of use.secrets)
export PAYMENT_API_KEY="your-api-key"
```

* [Runner Configuration Reference](lemline-ref-config.html)

# Metrics Reference

This reference lists the metrics Lemline exposes and where to read them.

## Endpoint

`lemline listen` and `lemline gateway start` serve Prometheus metrics over HTTP:

| Item |Value |
---------------
| URL |`http://<host>:<port>/q/metrics` |
| Port |`lemline.metrics.port` (default `8080`), or `--metrics-port` |
| Path |`lemline.metrics.path` (default `/q/metrics`) |

Health checks are served on the same port: `/q/health`, `/q/health/live` and `/q/health/ready`.

Other commands (`definition`, `instance start`, `config`, `migrate`, `failures replay`) do not expose metrics.

```BASH
curl http://localhost:8080/q/metrics
```

## Naming

Metrics are recorded with Micrometer and exported in Prometheus format. Dots become underscores, and timers are exported as `_seconds_count`, `_seconds_sum` and `_seconds_max`. For example:

| Micrometer name |Prometheus name |
------------------------------------
| `lemline.messaging.commands.received.total` |`lemline_messaging_commands_received_total` |
| `lemline.messaging.commands.processing.duration` |`lemline_messaging_commands_processing_duration_seconds_*` |

## Message Consumer Metrics

Each consumer of a runner records the same set of metrics under its own prefix:

| Prefix |Consumer |
--------------------
| `lemline.messaging.commands` |Workflow commands (workflow execution steps) |
| `lemline.messaging.events` |Workflow events (durable operations stored by the runner) |
| `lemline.messaging.cloudevents` |CloudEvents consumed for `listen` tasks |
| `lemline.analytics` |Lifecycle events ingested by lifecycle analytics |

For each `<prefix>`:

| Metric |Type |Tags |Description |
-----------------------------------
| `<prefix>.active` |Gauge |- |Messages being processed right now |
| `<prefix>.received.total` |Counter |- |Messages received |
| `<prefix>.deserialization.completed.total` |Counter |`workflow_name`, `workflow_version` |Messages decoded |
| `<prefix>.deserialization.failed.total` |Counter |`reason` |Messages that could not be decoded |
| `<prefix>.deserialization.duration` |Timer |- |Time spent decoding |
| `<prefix>.serialization.completed.total` |Counter |`workflow_name`, `workflow_version` |Messages encoded |
| `<prefix>.serialization.failed.total` |Counter |`reason`, `workflow_name`, `workflow_version` |Messages that could not be encoded |
| `<prefix>.serialization.duration` |Timer |- |Time spent encoding |
| `<prefix>.processing.completed.total` |Counter |`workflow_name`, `workflow_version` |Messages processed successfully |
| `<prefix>.processing.failed.total` |Counter |`reason`, `workflow_name`, `workflow_version` |Messages whose processing failed |
| `<prefix>.processing.duration` |Timer |`workflow_name`, `workflow_version` |Processing time, successful or not |
| `<prefix>.ack.completed.total` |Counter |`workflow_name`, `workflow_version` |Messages acknowledged to the broker |
| `<prefix>.ack.failed.total` |Counter |`reason`, `workflow_name`, `workflow_version` |Acknowledgements that failed |
| `<prefix>.nack.completed.total` |Counter |`workflow_name`, `workflow_version` |Messages rejected to the broker |
| `<prefix>.nack.failed.total` |Counter |`reason`, `workflow_name`, `workflow_version` |Rejections that failed |
| `<prefix>.foreign_namespace.total` |Counter |`workflow_namespace`, `workflow_name`, `workflow_version` |Messages received for a namespace this runner does not serve |

A rising `foreign_namespace.total` means messages reach a runner that is not configured for their namespace (see `lemline.namespaces`). Those messages are parked as failures and can be re-sent with `lemline failures replay`.

## Gateway Metrics

| Metric |Type |Tags |Description |
-----------------------------------
| `lemline.gateway.start.inactive_namespace.total` |Counter |`namespace` |Instances started in a namespace where no runner activity was recorded recently |

## Platform Metrics

Micrometer also exports its standard JVM and process metrics (memory, garbage collection, threads, CPU, uptime), with names such as `jvm_memory_used_bytes` and `process_cpu_usage`.

## Example Queries

```
# Commands processed per second, by workflow
sum by (workflow_name) (rate(lemline_messaging_commands_processing_completed_total[5m]))

# Failure ratio of command processing
sum(rate(lemline_messaging_commands_processing_failed_total[5m]))
  / sum(rate(lemline_messaging_commands_received_total[5m]))

# Average processing time
rate(lemline_messaging_commands_processing_duration_seconds_sum[5m])
  / rate(lemline_messaging_commands_processing_duration_seconds_count[5m])

# Messages in flight per runner
lemline_messaging_commands_active
```

## Related Resources

* [Runner Configuration Reference](lemline-ref-config.html)

* [Understanding Scaling in Lemline](lemline-explain-scaling.html)



# Lifecycle Analytics Reference

Lemline stores lifecycle CloudEvents in SQLite or PostgreSQL for historical queries and live watches through the gateway. Use SQLite for a local analytics file on a single host.

## What Lifecycle Analytics Does

When enabled, Lemline consumes lifecycle events and writes them to a dedicated analytics table.

* Input: lifecycle CloudEvents from the `lifecycleevents-in` channel

* Destination: the `lemline_lifecycle_events` table in the configured analytics database

* Deduplication key: `(source, event_id)`

* Payload: the complete serialized CloudEvent, including extensions and data, in `payload`

## Required Enablement

Lifecycle analytics requires both:

1. Lifecycle event production enabled

2. Lifecycle event consumer enabled

### Configure PostgreSQL

```YAML
lemline:
  messaging:
    type: kafka
    lifecycleevents:
      producer:
        enabled: true
      consumer:
        enabled: true
        concurrency: 64
    kafka:
      lifecycleevents:
        topic: lemline-lifecycle-events

  analytics:
    type: postgresql
    migrate-at-start: true
    baseline-on-migrate: false
    postgresql:
      host: localhost
      port: 5432
      database: lemline_analytics
      username: postgres
      password: postgres
      schema: lemline
```

Use a database dedicated to analytics. Its Flyway history is separate from the workflow database's, so pointing analytics at the workflow database and schema makes its first migration find a non-empty schema and stop the runner at startup (unless `baseline-on-migrate` is enabled).

`lemline listen` enables both the lifecycle event producer and consumer automatically. Configure the flags explicitly when running other processes that emit or ingest lifecycle events.

### Configure SQLite

For a new configuration, pass `--analytics sqlite` to `lemline config create` to store history in `analytics.db`. To configure an existing runner, set the analytics path in its YAML file:

```YAML
lemline:
  analytics:
    type: sqlite
    migrate-at-start: true
    sqlite:
      path: /var/lib/lemline/analytics.db
```

Set `type: sqlite` explicitly. If you omit `sqlite.path`, Lemline uses `analytics.db`. It resolves relative paths against the working directory of each process. Use a dedicated local file for analytics with an existing, writable parent directory. Use an absolute path when the runner and gateway start from different directories.

Start ingestion with `lemline --config lemline.yaml listen`. On the same host, configure the [gateway](lemline-ref-gateway.html) to use the same file and start it with `lemline --config lemline.yaml gateway start`. The gateway serves saved history with its analytics consumer disabled. When `migrate-at-start` is enabled, either process can prepare a new SQLite file. They take turns through an `analytics.db.migration.lock` file created next to the database; leave it in place. A gateway that creates a new file logs a warning, because a wrong path would otherwise show an empty history.

SQLite uses write-ahead logging (WAL), so gateway reads can continue while ingestion writes. SQLite serializes writes. Each connection enables foreign keys, uses `synchronous=FULL`, and waits up to five seconds for a database lock.

## Configuration Keys

| Property |Default |Description |
----------------------------------
| `lemline.messaging.lifecycleevents.consumer.enabled` |`false` |Enables lifecycle events consumer used for analytics ingestion |
| `lemline.messaging.<broker>.lifecycleevents.consumer.concurrency` |`64` |Max concurrent lifecycle analytics message handling (`lemline.messaging.lifecycleevents.consumer.concurrency` with in-memory messaging) |
| `lemline.analytics.type` |`h2` |Analytics backend. Choose `sqlite` or `postgresql`. `h2` is available in Lemline's test suite. |
| `lemline.analytics.sqlite.path` |`analytics.db` |Local SQLite database file. Used with `type: sqlite`. |
| `lemline.analytics.migrate-at-start` |`true` |Runs analytics Flyway migration on startup |
| `lemline.analytics.baseline-on-migrate` |`false` |Enables Flyway baseline behavior for PostgreSQL analytics |
| `lemline.analytics.postgresql.host` |`localhost` |Analytics PostgreSQL host |
| `lemline.analytics.postgresql.port` |`5432` |Analytics PostgreSQL port |
| `lemline.analytics.postgresql.database` |`lemline` |Analytics PostgreSQL database name; use a database separate from the workflow database |
| `lemline.analytics.postgresql.username` |`postgres` |Analytics PostgreSQL username |
| `lemline.analytics.postgresql.password` |`postgres` |Analytics PostgreSQL password |
| `lemline.analytics.postgresql.schema` |`lemline` |Target schema for lifecycle analytics table |
| `lemline.messaging.lifecycleevents.producer.enabled` |`false` |Enables emitting lifecycle events into the messaging layer |

## Analytics Table Shape

The table is `lemline_lifecycle_events` in SQLite and `lemline.lemline_lifecycle_events` by default in PostgreSQL.

Important columns:

* Event identity: `event_id`, `source`, `type`, `specversion`

* CloudEvent optional metadata: `subject`, `event_time`, `datacontenttype`, `dataschema`

* Workflow extensions: `lemline_workflow_id`, `lemline_workflow_namespace`, `lemline_workflow_name`, `lemline_workflow_version`

* Full payload: `payload` (JSON text in SQLite, `JSONB` in PostgreSQL)

* Ingestion timestamp: `ingested_at`

SQLite stores projected workflow IDs as lowercase UUID text and `event_time` and `ingested_at` as signed Unix epoch microseconds in UTC. A missing event time is SQL `NULL`. The original CloudEvent in `payload` retains its timestamp precision.

On every backend, `lemline_workflow_id` is filled only when the `lemlineworkflowid` extension is a complete UUID such as `01890a5d-ac96-774b-bcce-b302099a8057`, in either case. Lemline stores an event with any other value, logs a warning, and leaves the column `NULL`, so the gateway does not attach that event to an instance.

## Troubleshooting

* For SQLite startup errors, verify that the configured path names a local file and that the process can write to both the file and its parent directory. If you disabled `migrate-at-start`, start against an already migrated file.

* For PostgreSQL connectivity errors, verify `lemline.analytics.postgresql.*` and PostgreSQL availability.

* If no rows are inserted, verify both producer and consumer are enabled: * `lemline.messaging.lifecycleevents.producer.enabled=true` * `lemline.messaging.lifecycleevents.consumer.enabled=true`

* If rows are missing unexpectedly, check deduplication collisions on `(source, event_id)`.



# Lemline Implementation

## Error Handling Architecture

Lemline implements a 3-layer approach for handling error:

* Infrastructure Error: Failure during database access, broker access

* Lemline Error: Failures during serialization, deserialisation, and the processing of the workflow definition

* User Error: Failure during the processing of an activity that is non handled by the workflow definition

Note: If a failure is handled by the workflow definition (try/catch), Lemline does not see it as an error but a "normal"
processing of the workflow.

To avoid a coupling between the broker and the database, every upsert to the database is done through a `lemline_events`
topic. Also, this way insert in the database can done by batch.
If the database is not available when handling a message that needs it, the message will be saved in the
`lemline_events`
topic and retried later.

In that way, the broker is never blocked by the database unavailability.

## Instance Message Subscription

Generally speaking, Lemline will read a message and:

1. Deserialize the message

2. Retrieve the workflow definition (usually from local cache, if not present from database)

3. Init the workflow state, and run the workflow logic up to the next activity

4. Calls the activity

5. Update the workflow state and prepare the next message

6. Send the next message and acknowledge the previous message

The broker is supposedly a high-availability infrastructure, but we should consider the case when we do not manage to
send or (neg)acknowledge a message

## Error Handling

If Lemline encounters an error before 6., it will send the (idempotent) message to an `lemline_events` topic, with
additional info (status, stacktrace).

Once in the `lemline_retries` table, the message will be processed by a relay that will resend the message at a later
time.

## Scheduling

When starting a workflow, whose definition contains a `schedule` attribute, Lemline will

* send a (idempotent) message to the `lemline_events` topic with the workflow definition and the schedule

* start the workflow (if the schedule is not a cron) by sending a message to the `workflow` topic

Once in the `lemline_schedules` table, the message will be processed by a relay that will resend the message at a later
time.

## Child Workflows

When starting a child workflow, Lemline will:

* send a (idempotent) message to the `lemline_events` topic with the parent definition

* start the child workflow by sending a message to the `workflow` topic

When the child workflow is completed, Lemline will use the `lemline_parents` table to see if there is a parent
workflow waiting for the child workflow to complete.`Once in the`lemline_parents` table, the message will be processed by a relay that will resend the message at a later
time.

## Wait tasks

When starting a wait task, Lemline will

* send a (idempotent) message to the `lemline_events` topic with the delay.

Once in the `lemline_waits` table, the message will be processed by a relay that will resend the message at a later
time.

## Fork

TBD

## Ingestion Message Subscription

Another process inside Lemline reads those messages from the `lemline_events` topic and save them to different tables
depending on their nature:

* the `lemline_retries` table

* the `lemline_parents` table

* the `lemline_schedules` table

* the `lemline_waits` table

Lemline bulk inserts the messages into the database.

1. Once sending this message succeeds, the initial message is acknowledged

2. if an error occurs during acknowledgement, Lemline will retry until it succeeds

save the workflow state into the `lemline_retries` table, with a status `FAILED` if the error is unrecoverable, or
`PENDING` if the error could be transient

1. If saving this message fails (eg. database down or network issue), then the message is negatively acknowledged

2. If saving this message succeeds, then the message is acknowledged

3. If Lemline does not manage to acknowledge or (neg-acknowledge) the message, it keeps trying until successfully doing
it (in case or broker downtime or network issue)

In 1. the saved state of the message will be:

* the unmodified state of the message if the error occurs before or during the activity processing

* the state updated if the error occurs during after the activity processing

## Error Status Definitions

* Failed: Messages that cannot be processed due to permanent issues (malformed data, missing definitions)

* Pending: Messages that failed due to transient issues (database connectivity, external service timeouts)

Failed messages should be human reviewed and potentially retried manually.

### Error Handling Strategy

Each step has specific error handling to ensure message reliability and system stability:

#### Deserialization Errors (Step 1)

* Action: Save the raw message payload to database as "failed"

* Message Handling: Acknowledge the message (remove from queue)

* Rationale: Malformed messages cannot be processed and should not block the queue

#### Workflow Definition Errors (Step 2)

* Action: If definition not found, throw error and rely on dead letter queue

* Action: If database access fails, save message for retry

* Message Handling: Negative acknowledgment for database failures, dead letter queue for missing definitions

* Rationale: Missing definitions require human intervention, database failures may be transient

#### Workflow Execution Errors (Step 3)

* Action: Save the current workflow state to database for "manual introspection"

* Message Handling: Acknowledge the message

* Rationale: Workflow logic is deterministic - retrying won't change the outcome

#### Activity Processing Errors (Step 4)

* Action: Save the message to database marked for "retry"

* Message Handling: Acknowledge the message

* Rationale: Activity failures may be transient and worth retrying

#### Serialization Errors (Steps 5 & 6)

* Action: Save the current state or original message to database

* Message Handling: Acknowledge the message

* Rationale: Serialization issues indicate data corruption, not transient failures

### Message Acknowledgment Strategy

* Positive Acknowledgment: Message is removed from the queue after successful processing or error handling

* Negative Acknowledgment: Only used when the error handling itself fails (e.g., database connection issues)

### Crash Recovery Design

To ensure message processing survives application crashes:

* Deterministic IDs: All database IDs and message IDs are deterministically generated from the original message ID

* Benefit: Prevents duplicate processing and ensures consistent state recovery after restarts

* Implementation: Uses hash-based ID generation to maintain consistency across application instances

### Key Principles

1. No Message Loss: Every message is either processed successfully or saved for review/retry

2. Queue Health: Failed messages are acknowledged to prevent queue blocking

3. Audit Trail: All errors are logged with sufficient context for debugging

4. Recovery Ready: System can resume processing from any point after a restart

## Retries

if a message need to be be retried, this content is saved into the lemline_retries table. Then all running lemline
applications request this table regularly to

* select the pending



# Gateway Reference

This reference documents the current public `lemline-runner-gateway` API: RPC surface, cursor and watch semantics, start idempotency, security rules, and configuration required to run the gateway.

## Overview

`lemline-runner-gateway` is Lemline's public gRPC ingress and read API for:

1. workflow definition catalog access

2. definition-level execution statistics

3. workflow instance start and listing

4. per-instance lifecycle event timelines

The gateway is not started as a standalone module. It is loaded by `lemline-runner` and started with:

```BASH
lemline gateway start
```

It shares the same `.lemline.yaml` configuration model as the runner and depends on:

1. runner database configuration for gateway outbox persistence

2. runner messaging configuration to publish workflow start commands

3. analytics configuration for read-side queries and watch streams

For a first request, follow [Start and follow an order through the gRPC gateway](lemline-tutorial-gateway.html). For a shared installation, see [Deploy the gRPC gateway](lemline-howto-deploy-gateway.html).

The dashboard is an optional web client. See [Connect the dashboard to the gateway](lemline-howto-connect-dashboard.html) for browser transport and authentication.

## Service Contract

Service: `lemline.gateway.v1.GatewayService`

### Common Conventions

* `List*` RPCs return finite snapshots.

* `Get*` RPCs return exactly one resource.

* `Watch*` RPCs return live streams.

* Cursors are opaque and scoped to one RPC plus the exact filter set that produced them.

* When a paginated list response includes `watch_cursor`, every page from that snapshot returns the same cursor. Consume the final page before using that cursor with the corresponding `Watch*` RPC.

* All time windows use `[from, to)` semantics: inclusive lower bound, exclusive upper bound.

* `page_size = 0` lets the server choose a default page size.

### RPC Surface

| RPC |Request |Response |Current behavior |
--------------------------------------------
| `ListDefinitions` |`ListDefinitionsRequest` |`ListDefinitionsResponse` |Returns a finite catalog snapshot ordered by `namespace ASC`, `name ASC`, `version DESC`. `latest_only` defaults to `true` when omitted. |
| `GetDefinition` |`GetDefinitionRequest` |`GetDefinitionResponse` |Returns one full definition. If `version` is omitted, the latest version for `namespace/name` is returned. |
| `ListDefinitionStats` |`ListDefinitionStatsRequest` |`ListDefinitionStatsResponse` |Returns finite definition-level counters for a time window. `time_from` is required; omit `time_to` for an open window that follows the latest lifecycle events. Includes `watch_cursor` for snapshot-then-tail flows. |
| `WatchDefinitionStats` |`WatchDefinitionStatsRequest` |`stream WatchDefinitionStatsResponse` |Delta stream of `UPSERT` and `REMOVED` changes for definition stats. If `after_cursor` is omitted, the stream starts from "now" and emits only future changes. With `time_to` omitted, counters keep moving as new instances start and finish. A client resuming from a change in the middle of one update may receive that update's changes again; each change carries the row's full state. |
| `StartInstance` |`StartInstanceRequest` |`StartInstanceResponse` |Starts a workflow instance asynchronously. If `instance_id` is omitted, the server generates a UUIDv7 identifier. If `version` is omitted, the latest definition version is started. |
| `GetInstance` |`GetInstanceRequest` |`GetInstanceResponse` |Returns the current instance summary and, when known, a `latest_event_cursor` that can be used to tail events without replaying older ones. |
| `ListInstances` |`ListInstancesRequest` |`ListInstancesResponse` |Returns a finite instance snapshot ordered by `created_at DESC`, `instance_id DESC`. Includes `watch_cursor` for snapshot-then-tail flows. |
| `WatchInstances` |`WatchInstancesRequest` |`stream WatchInstancesResponse` |Delta stream of `UPSERT` and `REMOVED` changes to the filtered instance set. If `after_cursor` is omitted, the stream starts from "now" and emits only future changes. |
| `ListInstanceEvents` |`ListInstanceEventsRequest` |`ListInstanceEventsResponse` |Returns finite ordered history for one instance, in ascending event-cursor order. |
| `WatchInstanceEvents` |`WatchInstanceEventsRequest` |`stream WatchInstanceEventsResponse` |Streams one instance timeline. If `after_cursor` is omitted, the server replays from the first event and then tails live events. |
| `GetGatewayConfig` |`GetGatewayConfigRequest` |`GetGatewayConfigResponse` |Returns the configuration the gateway runs with, where each value comes from, and the configuration file as read at startup. Secret values are never returned. |

### StartInstance Request and Response

`StartInstanceRequest`:

| Field |Required |Description |
--------------------------------
| `namespace` |yes |Target definition namespace |
| `name` |yes |Target definition name |
| `version` |no |Concrete definition version; omitted means latest |
| `instance_id` |no |Caller-supplied UUIDv7 string for idempotent starts |
| `input` |no |Workflow input as `google.protobuf.Value`; omitted behaves as `{}` |
| `zone_id` |no |IANA time zone ID; omitted or blank defaults to `UTC` |

`StartInstanceResponse`:

| Field |Description |
----------------------
| `instance_id` |Created or reused instance identifier |
| `namespace` |Resolved definition namespace |
| `name` |Resolved definition name |
| `version` |Resolved definition version actually started |
| `result` |`START_INSTANCE_RESULT_ACCEPTED_NEW` or `START_INSTANCE_RESULT_ACCEPTED_EXISTING` |

### Resource Shapes

* `WorkflowDefinition` returns the stored definition `source`, the resolved `version`, and `available_versions` ordered newest first.

* `DefinitionStats` returns `started_count`, `completed_count`, `faulted_count`, and `running_count_at_time_to` (running at `time_to`, or at the latest lifecycle event when `time_to` is omitted) for one `namespace/name/version`.

* `InstanceSummary` returns the resolved definition identity, lifecycle status, timestamps, optional `duration`, and optional structured `error`.

* `InstanceEvent` returns an opaque per-instance `cursor`, normalized `event_type`, optional `event_time`, and canonical `cloud_event_json`.

## Execution Semantics

### Start Idempotency

`StartInstance` is idempotent when the caller supplies `instance_id`.

* First accepted request for an `instance_id`: returns `START_INSTANCE_RESULT_ACCEPTED_NEW`

* Same `instance_id` with the same effective start parameters: returns `START_INSTANCE_RESULT_ACCEPTED_EXISTING`

* Same `instance_id` with different effective parameters: rejected with `ALREADY_EXISTS`

Current conflict detection compares:

1. resolved workflow identity (`namespace`, `name`, resolved `version`)

2. normalized workflow input

3. schedule zone when schedule-based persistence is involved

Additional request behavior:

* If `instance_id` is omitted, the gateway generates a UUIDv7 identifier.

* If `input` is omitted, the server behaves as if `{}` was supplied.

* If `input` is present but does not contain a JSON value, the request is rejected.

* If `zone_id` is invalid, the request is rejected with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.

### List and Watch Pairing

For definition stats and instances, the intended no-gap client pattern is:

1. call the corresponding `List*` RPC

2. consume all pages from that snapshot

3. pass the returned `watch_cursor` into the matching `Watch*` RPC

Current watch semantics differ by resource:

* `WatchDefinitionStats`: delta stream, future-only when `after_cursor` is omitted

* `WatchInstances`: delta stream, future-only when `after_cursor` is omitted

* `WatchInstanceEvents`: replay-first stream, replays from the first event when `after_cursor` is omitted

### Instance Event Access

`GetInstance`, `ListInstanceEvents`, and `WatchInstanceEvents` authorize read access by namespace.

Current implementation resolves that namespace from:

1. the latest instance summary when available

2. otherwise the first lifecycle event for the instance

If neither exists, the gateway returns `NOT_FOUND`.

## Security Model

Transport security and request authentication are configured separately:

1. TLS is controlled by `lemline.gateway.tls.*`

2. client certificate mode is controlled by `lemline.gateway.tls.client-auth` (`none`, `request`, `required`)

3. bearer JWT authentication and authorization are controlled by `lemline.gateway.authentication.*`

Validation and runtime rules:

* `lemline.gateway.authentication.enabled=true` requires `lemline.gateway.tls.enabled=true`

* when TLS is enabled, `certificate` and `private-key` are required

* when client auth is `request` or `required`, `trust-store` is required

* when authentication is enabled, `jwt.issuer` and `jwt.jwks-url` are required

* when authentication is enabled and no authenticated principal is available, the RPC fails with `UNAUTHENTICATED`

* when authentication is disabled, the gateway allows all scopes. It serves the namespaces configured for the process, or all namespaces when none are configured.

Current scope requirements:

* `lemline.start` for `StartInstance`

* `lemline.watch` for `WatchDefinitionStats`

* `lemline.watch` for `WatchInstances`

* `lemline.watch` for `WatchInstanceEvents`

* `lemline.config` for `GetGatewayConfig`

Current namespace rules:

* other non-streaming read RPCs do not require a scope

* namespace authorization is still enforced for read RPCs when authentication is enabled

* `List*` calls without an explicit namespace are automatically limited to the caller's allowed namespaces

* `*` in the namespaces claim allows access to all namespaces

Default claim names:

* scopes claim: `scope`

* namespaces claim: `lemline_namespaces`

Supply the scope and namespace claims as strings. Separate multiple values with spaces or commas.

## Error Mapping

| Condition |gRPC status |
--------------------------
| Missing authenticated principal when authentication is enabled |`UNAUTHENTICATED` |
| Invalid request fields, invalid UUIDv7, invalid timezone, invalid cursors, or invalid time ranges |`INVALID_ARGUMENT` |
| Missing definition or instance |`NOT_FOUND` |
| Duplicate `instance_id` with conflicting effective parameters |`ALREADY_EXISTS` |
| Missing scope or namespace authorization |`PERMISSION_DENIED` |
| Unhandled internal failure |`INTERNAL` |

## Configuration

### Config File Resolution

Gateway startup uses the same config resolution order as `lemline-runner`:

1. `--config=<path>` or `-c <path>`

2. `LEMLINE_CONFIG`

3. `./.lemline.yaml`

4. `~/.config/lemline/config.yaml`

5. `~/.lemline.yaml`

### Gateway Keys

| Property |Default |Required |Description |
--------------------------------------------
| `lemline.gateway.enabled` |`false` |no |Enables gateway server startup |
| `lemline.gateway.grpc.host` |`0.0.0.0` |no |gRPC bind host |
| `lemline.gateway.grpc.port` |`9000` |no |gRPC bind port |
| `lemline.gateway.cors.enabled` |`true` |no |Enables CORS for browser and gRPC-Web clients |
| `lemline.gateway.cors.origins` |`http://localhost:5173` |no |Allowed CORS origins |
| `lemline.gateway.cors.methods` |`GET,POST,OPTIONS` |no |Allowed CORS methods |
| `lemline.gateway.cors.headers` |`Accept,Authorization,Content-Type,Grpc-Timeout,X-Grpc-Web,X-User-Agent` |no |Allowed CORS request headers |
| `lemline.gateway.tls.enabled` |`true` |no |Enables TLS for the gRPC server |
| `lemline.gateway.tls.certificate` |- |yes if `tls.enabled=true` |Server certificate path |
| `lemline.gateway.tls.private-key` |- |yes if `tls.enabled=true` |Server private key path |
| `lemline.gateway.tls.client-auth` |`none` |no |mTLS mode: `none`, `request`, or `required` |
| `lemline.gateway.tls.trust-store` |- |yes if `client-auth` is `request` or `required` |Trust store used for client certificate validation |
| `lemline.gateway.tls.trust-store-password` |- |depends on store |Trust store password |
| `lemline.gateway.authentication.enabled` |`true` |no |Enables JWT authentication and authorization |
| `lemline.gateway.authentication.jwt.issuer` |- |yes if `authentication.enabled=true` |Expected JWT issuer |
| `lemline.gateway.authentication.jwt.jwks-url` |- |yes if `authentication.enabled=true` |JWKS URL used for JWT validation |
| `lemline.gateway.authentication.claims.scope-field` |`scope` |no |JWT claim name for scopes |
| `lemline.gateway.authentication.claims.namespaces-field` |`lemline_namespaces` |no |JWT claim name for allowed namespaces |
| `lemline.gateway.watch.poll-interval-ms` |`250` |no |Watch polling interval in milliseconds |
| `lemline.gateway.watch.batch-size` |`256` |no |Maximum rows fetched per watch poll |

Notes:

1. `lemline gateway start` sets `lemline.gateway.enabled=true` automatically; keeping it in config is still fine.

2. Authentication cannot be enabled on plaintext transport.

### Analytics Keys for Read APIs

Definition stats, instance reads, and instance-event timelines are backed by the analytics lifecycle-event store.

The gateway can read from PostgreSQL, SQLite on the JVM, and H2 in Lemline's test suite.

| Property |Default |Description |
----------------------------------
| `lemline.analytics.type` |`h2` |Analytics backend selector |
| `lemline.analytics.sqlite.path` |`analytics.db` |SQLite analytics file shared with the runner on the same host |
| `lemline.analytics.migrate-at-start` |`true` |Analytics migration toggle |
| `lemline.analytics.baseline-on-migrate` |`false` |PostgreSQL analytics Flyway baseline toggle |
| `lemline.analytics.postgresql.host` |`localhost` |PostgreSQL host |
| `lemline.analytics.postgresql.port` |`5432` |PostgreSQL port |
| `lemline.analytics.postgresql.database` |`lemline` |PostgreSQL database name |
| `lemline.analytics.postgresql.username` |`postgres` |PostgreSQL user |
| `lemline.analytics.postgresql.password` |`postgres` |PostgreSQL password |
| `lemline.analytics.postgresql.schema` |`lemline` |Lifecycle-events schema |

The gateway requires a reachable analytics datasource at startup. Lemline configures the datasource when either the gateway or the lifecycle event consumer is enabled.

* For PostgreSQL analytics, configure `lemline.analytics.type=postgresql` and the `lemline.analytics.postgresql.*` settings.

* For SQLite analytics, configure `lemline.analytics.type=sqlite` and point `lemline.analytics.sqlite.path` at the lifecycle analytics file. The gateway prepares the SQLite schema at startup when `migrate-at-start` is enabled, including with the analytics consumer disabled. See [Lifecycle Analytics Reference](lemline-ref-analytics.html).

### Minimal Local Development Example

Use this only on trusted local networks:

```YAML
lemline:
  gateway:
    enabled: true
    grpc:
      host: 127.0.0.1
      port: 9000
    cors:
      enabled: true
      origins: http://localhost:5173
    tls:
      enabled: false
    authentication:
      enabled: false

  analytics:
    type: postgresql
    migrate-at-start: true
    baseline-on-migrate: false
    postgresql:
      host: localhost
      port: 5432
      database: lemline
      username: postgres
      password: postgres
      schema: lemline
```

## Build and Run

Build:

```BASH
./gradlew :lemline-runner:build
```

Run the JVM package:

```BASH
java -jar lemline-runner/build/quarkus-app/quarkus-run.jar --config=/absolute/path/.lemline.yaml gateway start
```

Build a native package:

```BASH
./gradlew :lemline-runner:assemble -Dquarkus.native.enabled=true -Dquarkus.package.jar.enabled=false
```

Run the native binary:

```BASH
./lemline-runner/build/lemline-runner-*-runner --config=/absolute/path/.lemline.yaml gateway start
```



# Command Syntax and Options

This reference lists every command of the Lemline command-line interface, with its options and examples.

## CLI Overview

The `lemline` command lets you:

* register, read and delete workflow definitions

* start workflow instances

* run runners (`listen`) and the gRPC gateway (`gateway start`)

* create and inspect the configuration

* apply database migrations

* replay messages parked as failures

Instances are observed through the gateway and the dashboard; the CLI has no command to list, cancel, suspend or resume instances.

## Basic Syntax

```
lemline <command> [<subcommand>] [options] [arguments]
```

## Global Options

These options are accepted by every command and subcommand:

| Option |Description |
-----------------------
| `-h`, `--help` |Show help for the command |
| `-V`, `--version` |Show the Lemline version |
| `-c`, `--config <path>` |Configuration file to use (see [Configuring the Lemline Runner](lemline-howto-config.html)) |
| `--debug`, `--info`, `--warn`, `--error` |Set the log level (default: `ERROR`) |
| `--json` |Write logs in JSON |

## Commands

| Command |Purpose |
--------------------
| `definition get` |Show or list workflow definitions |
| `definition post` |Register workflow definitions from files |
| `definition delete` |Delete workflow definitions |
| `instance start` |Start a workflow instance |
| `listen` |Run a runner: consume messages and execute workflows |
| `gateway start` |Run the gRPC gateway |
| `config show` |Print the effective configuration |
| `config create` |Generate a configuration file |
| `migrate` |Apply pending database migrations |
| `migrate status` |Show the state of database migrations |
| `failures replay` |Re-send messages parked as failures |

### 

`definition get`

```
lemline definition get [<namespace> [<name> [<version>]]] [-f yaml|json]
```

* With namespace, name and version: prints that definition.

* Otherwise: lists the matching definitions and lets you pick one by number (`q` quits). When only one matches, it is printed directly.

| Option |Description |Default |
--------------------------------
| `-f`, `--format` |`yaml` or `json` |`yaml` |

```BASH
# List all definitions
lemline definition get

# Print one version as JSON
lemline definition get default order-processing 1.0.0 --format json
```

### 

`definition post`

```
lemline definition post (-f <file> | -d <directory>) [-r] [-F]
```

Registers the definitions found in the given files. The namespace, name and version come from each file's `document` section.

| Option |Description |
-----------------------
| `-f`, `--file <path>` |A definition file (repeatable) |
| `-d`, `--directory <path>` |A directory of definition files (repeatable) |
| `-r`, `--recursive` |Also read subdirectories |
| `-F`, `--force` |Replace a definition that already exists with the same name and version |

```BASH
lemline definition post -f order-processing.yaml
lemline definition post -d ./workflows -r
```

### 

`definition delete`

```
lemline definition delete <namespace> [<name> [<version>]] [-F]
```

Without `--force`, lists the matching definitions, lets you pick one (or `*` for all of them) and asks for confirmation. With `--force`, deletes without asking:

* `<namespace>`: every definition of the namespace

* `<namespace> <name>`: every version of that workflow

* `<namespace> <name> <version>`: that version only

```BASH
lemline definition delete default order-processing 1.0.0
```

### 

`instance start`

```
lemline instance start <namespace> <name> [<version>] [-i <json>] [-z <timezone>]
```

Starts a new instance and prints its id. Without a version, the latest version is used.

| Option |Description |Default |
--------------------------------
| `-i`, `--input <json>` |Workflow input, as JSON |`{}` |
| `-z`, `--zone <timezone>` |Time zone used by the workflow schedule, e.g. `Europe/Paris` |system time zone |

```BASH
lemline instance start default order-processing --input '{"orderId": "123"}'
```

The command returns once the instance is started; it does not wait for the result.

### 

`listen`

```
lemline listen [-m <port>] [--mock-config <file>]
```

Runs a runner until it is stopped. The runner consumes commands, events and CloudEvents for its namespaces, executes workflows and runs the background tasks (waits, retries, schedules, cleanup).

| Option |Description |Default |
--------------------------------
| `-m`, `--metrics-port <port>` |Port of the metrics and health endpoints |`lemline.metrics.port` (`8080`) |
| `--mock-config <file>` |YAML or JSON file of mocked activity responses; turns on test mode |- |

### 

`gateway start`

```
lemline gateway start [-g <port>] [-m <port>]
```

Runs the gRPC gateway until it is stopped. See [gRPC Gateway Reference](lemline-ref-gateway.html).

| Option |Description |Default |
--------------------------------
| `-g`, `--grpc-port <port>` |gRPC port |`lemline.gateway.grpc.port` (`9000`) |
| `-m`, `--metrics-port <port>` |Port of the metrics and health endpoints |`lemline.metrics.port` (`8080`) |

### 

`config show`

```
lemline config show [-f yaml|properties] [-a]
```

Prints the configuration Lemline will use, after merging the file, environment variables and system properties.

| Option |Description |Default |
--------------------------------
| `-f`, `--format` |`yaml` or `properties` |`yaml` |
| `-a`, `--all` |Include non-`lemline.*` properties |off |

### 

`config create`

```
lemline config create [-m <broker>] [-d <database>] [--analytics <type>] [-o <path>] [--force] [--dry-run]
```

Run `lemline config create -o .lemline.yaml` in a terminal to choose messaging, orchestration and analytics in order. Press Enter at the analytics prompt to accept the displayed default. Lemline reads `.lemline.yaml` automatically from the current directory.

For scripts, supply both `--messaging` and `--database`. With both options present, the command runs without prompts. Use `--analytics` to select the history database explicitly. If you use the default output name, pass `--config lemline.yaml` to subsequent commands.

| Option |Description |Default |
--------------------------------
| `-m`, `--messaging` |`kafka`, `rabbitmq`, `pgmq` or `sqlite` |asked |
| `-d`, `--database` |Orchestration database: `postgresql`, `mysql` or `sqlite` |asked |
| `--analytics` |Workflow history database: `postgresql` or `sqlite` |See defaults below. |
| `-o`, `--output <path>` |File to write |`lemline.yaml` |
| `--force` |Overwrite an existing file |off |
| `--dry-run` |Print the file instead of writing it |off |

With `--analytics` omitted, the generated YAML follows these defaults.

| Messaging |Orchestration |Generated analytics section |
---------------------------------------------------------
| SQLite |SQLite |SQLite file at `analytics.db` |
| SQLite |PostgreSQL or MySQL |PostgreSQL |
| Kafka, RabbitMQ or PGMQ |Any |Section omitted |

### 

`migrate`

```
lemline migrate [--pretend] [--force]
lemline migrate status
```

`migrate` lists pending database migrations, asks for confirmation and applies them. `migrate status` prints every migration with its state.

| Option |Description |
-----------------------
| `--pretend` |List pending migrations without applying them |
| `--force` |Apply without asking for confirmation |

### 

`failures replay`

```
lemline failures replay [--id <uuid> | --reason <reason>] [--dry-run] [-y]
```

Re-sends messages that were parked in the failures table to their broker destination. Rows sent successfully are deleted; rows that cannot be decoded are reported and kept.

| Option |Description |Default |
--------------------------------
| `--id <uuid>` |Replay a single failure |- |
| `--reason <reason>` |Replay every failure with this reason |`foreign_namespace` |
| `--dry-run` |List what would be replayed |off |
| `-y`, `--yes` |Do not ask for confirmation |off |

## Environment Variables

| Variable |Description |
-------------------------
| `LEMLINE_CONFIG` |Configuration file to use when `--config` is not given |

Every configuration property can also be set as an environment variable. See [Environment Variables Reference](lemline-ref-env-vars.html).

## Related Resources

* [Configuring the Lemline Runner](lemline-howto-config.html)

* [Runner Configuration Reference](lemline-ref-config.html)

* [gRPC Gateway Reference](lemline-ref-gateway.html)



# Error Reference

This reference documents the standard error types and error handling capabilities in Lemline.

## Standard Error Types

Lemline implements the standardized error types defined in the Open Workflow Specification, with the base URI `https://open-workflow-specification.org/spec/1.0.0/errors/`:

| Error Type |URI |Default Status |Description |
------------------------------------------------
| Configuration |`https://open-workflow-specification.org/spec/1.0.0/errors/configuration` |400 |Errors in workflow definition or structure |
| Validation |`https://open-workflow-specification.org/spec/1.0.0/errors/validation` |400 |Input/output data schema validation failures |
| Expression |`https://open-workflow-specification.org/spec/1.0.0/errors/expression` |400 |Expression evaluation errors (JQ syntax or execution) |
| Authentication |`https://open-workflow-specification.org/spec/1.0.0/errors/authentication` |401 |Authentication failures |
| Authorization |`https://open-workflow-specification.org/spec/1.0.0/errors/authorization` |403 |Authorization/permission failures |
| Timeout |`https://open-workflow-specification.org/spec/1.0.0/errors/timeout` |408 |Timeout violations (workflow or task) |
| Communication |`https://open-workflow-specification.org/spec/1.0.0/errors/communication` |500 |Errors communicating with external services |
| Runtime |`https://open-workflow-specification.org/spec/1.0.0/errors/runtime` |500 |General runtime execution errors |

## Error Structure

All errors in Lemline follow the RFC 7807 Problem Details format:

```JSON
{
  "type": "https://open-workflow-specification.org/spec/1.0.0/errors/validation",
  "status": 400,
  "instance": "/do/0/validateInput",
  "title": "Input Validation Failed",
  "detail": "The 'amount' field must be a positive number"
}
```

| Field |Required |Description |
--------------------------------
| `type` |Yes |URI reference identifying the problem type |
| `status` |Yes |HTTP status code (numeric) corresponding to the error |
| `instance` |Yes |JSON pointer to the location in the workflow where the error occurred |
| `title` |No |Short, human-readable summary of the problem |
| `detail` |No |Detailed explanation specific to this error occurrence |

## Error Titles and Details

Lemline errors carry no numeric or symbolic error code: identify them by `type` (and `status`), and read `title` and `detail` for the specific cause. For example:

| Situation |`type` |`status` |Example message |
------------------------------------------------
| A declared secret is not set on the runner |`authorization` |403 |`Required secret 'API_KEY' is unavailable` |
| An HTTP call returns a non-2xx status |`communication` |the HTTP status (for example 404) |`HTTP 404: <response body>` |
| An HTTP call gets no response (unknown host, refused connection, timeout) |`communication` |500 |`Unable to reach https://api.example.com: unresolved host` |
| An A2A call gets a non-2xx status from the agent |`communication` (see below) |the HTTP status |title `A2A message/send failed`, `detail` `HTTP 503: <response body>` |
| An A2A call gets no usable answer (unreachable agent, timeout, stream cut before its final result) |`communication` (see below) |500 |title `A2A message/send failed`, `detail` `Unable to reach https://agent.example.com: ...` |
| A `listen` task reaches its timeout |`timeout` |408 |`Listen task timed out at ...` |
| An expression fails to evaluate |`expression` |400 |the evaluation error message |
| Input or output does not match its schema |`validation` |400 |the schema validation message |

A failed HTTP call can therefore be caught by type and by status, for example `catch.errors.with: { type: https://open-workflow-specification.org/spec/1.0.0/errors/communication, status: 503 }`. The `Unable to reach` title names the server only, never the path or the query of the URL.

Errors raised by `call: a2a` use the base URI `https://serverlessworkflow.io/spec/1.0.0/errors/` instead: catch `https://serverlessworkflow.io/spec/1.0.0/errors/communication` for the failures above, and `https://serverlessworkflow.io/spec/1.0.0/errors/runtime` for the others, such as an error returned by the agent in its JSON-RPC answer.

Lemline only raises `timeout` errors for `listen` tasks: workflow-level timeouts and timeouts on other tasks are not enforced yet.

## CLI Exit Codes

| Exit Code |Description |
--------------------------
| 0 |Success |
| 1 |Error while running the command (including a missing configuration file) |
| 2 |Invalid command line (unknown option, missing argument) |

## Gateway API Errors

The gateway exposes gRPC (and Connect) APIs. Failed calls return standard gRPC status codes, for example `INVALID_ARGUMENT` for an invalid request, `NOT_FOUND` for an unknown definition or instance, `ALREADY_EXISTS`, `UNAUTHENTICATED`, `PERMISSION_DENIED` and `INTERNAL`.

## Java Exception Hierarchy

For developers working on Lemline, workflow errors are carried by a single exception type:

```
java.lang.RuntimeException
└── com.lemline.core.errors.WorkflowException (sealed)
    └── com.lemline.core.errors.InternalException
```

An activity reports a failed exchange with an external service by throwing `com.lemline.core.errors.CommunicationException`, which carries the status to report; it becomes a `communication` error. Any other exception thrown by an activity becomes a `runtime` error with status 500.

`InternalException` holds an `InternalException.Error` with the standard error fields (`type`, `status`, `instance`, `title`, `detail`). The error type is one of the values of `com.lemline.core.errors.WorkflowErrorType` (`configuration`, `validation`, `expression`, `authentication`, `authorization`, `timeout`, `communication`, `runtime`).

## Defining Custom Errors

Custom error types can be defined in workflow definitions:

```YAML
document:
  dsl: '1.0.3'
  namespace: examples
  name: typed-error
  version: '1.0.0'
use:
  errors:
    invalidOrder:
      type: https://errors.example.com/invalid-order
      status: 422
      title: Invalid order
do:
  - validateOrder:
      if: ${ (.orderId // "") == "" }
      raise:
        error: invalidOrder
  - acceptOrder:
      set:
        status: accepted
```

## Error Handling Examples

### Basic Try-Catch

```YAML
document:
  dsl: 1.0.3
  namespace: examples
  name: basic-try-catch
  version: 1.0.0
do:
  - secureOperation:
      try:
        - riskyTask:
            listen:
              to:
                one:
                  with:
                    type: com.example.payment.received
            timeout:
              after:
                seconds: 5
      catch:
        errors:
          with:
            type: https://open-workflow-specification.org/spec/1.0.0/errors/timeout
        as: timeoutError
        do:
          - handleTimeout:
              set:
                processed: false
                reason: ${ $timeoutError.title }
```

### Matching Multiple Error Types

A `try` task has a single `catch`. To handle several errors differently, catch them and route on the fields of the caught error in `catch.do`:

```YAML
document:
  dsl: '1.0.3'
  namespace: examples
  name: matching-multiple-error-types
  version: '1.0.0'
do:
  - callService:
      try:
        - request:
            call: http
            with:
              method: get
              endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:8787/products
              query:
                fail: ${ .failStatus | tostring }
      catch:
        as: error
        do:
          - routeByStatus:
              switch:
                - rateLimited:
                    when: ${ $error.status == 429 }
                    then: handleRateLimit
                - unavailable:
                    when: ${ $error.status == 503 }
                    then: handleUnavailable
                - default:
                    then: handleOtherError
          - handleRateLimit:
              set:
                outcome: rate-limited
              then: exit
          - handleUnavailable:
              set:
                outcome: unavailable
              then: exit
          - handleOtherError:
              set:
                outcome: failed
                errorType: ${ $error.type }
```

### Using Retry Policies

```YAML
document:
  dsl: 1.0.3
  namespace: examples
  name: using-retry-policies
  version: 1.0.0
do:
  - readStock:
      try:
        - operation:
            call: http
            with:
              method: get
              endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:8787/stock
              query:
                fail: '503'
                failTimes: '1'
                key: ${ $workflow.id }
      catch:
        retry:
          delay:
            seconds: 1
          backoff:
            exponential: {}
          limit:
            attempt:
              count: 3
          when: ${ $error.status >= 500 }
```

## Error Debugging

When debugging errors:

* Read the `workflow.faulted` and `task.faulted` lifecycle events of the instance in the dashboard; they carry the error `type`, `status`, `title`, `instance` (position in the workflow) and `detail`.

* Run the runner with `--debug` to log the input of each task. Every log line carries the workflow namespace, name, version and instance id, so you can filter on the instance.

## Error Handling Best Practices

1. Be specific with error types: Catch specific error types rather than all errors

2. Provide fallbacks: Use default values or alternative paths for common errors

3. Use conditional retries: Only retry errors that have a chance of succeeding on retry

4. Include context in errors: Use descriptive error messages with relevant details

5. Log error details: Log sufficient context for debugging

6. Use appropriate error status codes: Match HTTP status codes to semantics

7. Define custom error types: Create domain-specific error types for your application

8. Organize errors hierarchically: Use consistent type URIs that reflect hierarchy

## Run the Examples

Every example on this page is a complete workflow. Complete [the SQLite setup](lemline-tutorial-setup.html), save each example under the file name used below, and run the commands from the setup directory. With the JAR, substitute `java -jar lemline.jar` for `bin/lemline`.

Start the [tutorial shop](lemline-tutorial-order-processing.html#start-the-tutorial-shop) from the root of the Lemline source checkout:

```BASH
docker compose -f examples/tutorial-services/compose.yaml up -d
```

Keep the setup worker running and use a second terminal in the setup directory.

```BASH
bin/lemline definition post -f typed-error.yaml
bin/lemline instance start examples typed-error
bin/lemline definition post -f basic-try-catch.yaml
bin/lemline instance start examples basic-try-catch
bin/lemline definition post -f matching-multiple-error-types.yaml
bin/lemline instance start examples matching-multiple-error-types --input '{"failStatus":429}'
bin/lemline instance start examples matching-multiple-error-types --input '{"failStatus":503}'
bin/lemline instance start examples matching-multiple-error-types --input '{"failStatus":404}'
bin/lemline definition post -f using-retry-policies.yaml
bin/lemline instance start examples using-retry-policies
```

| Example |Expected result |
----------------------------
| `typed-error` |Faults with `invalid-order`, status 422 |
| `basic-try-catch` |After 5 to 15 seconds, `{"processed":false,"reason":"Listen task timed out"}` |
| `matching-multiple-error-types` |`{"outcome":"rate-limited"}`, `{"outcome":"unavailable"}`, then `{"outcome":"failed"}` with the `communication` error type |
| `using-retry-policies` |The stock after one retry: the HTTP 503 has status 503, so `when` holds |

Stop the shop when you are done:

```BASH
docker compose -f examples/tutorial-services/compose.yaml down
```

# Authentication Reference

Authentication policies are part of the Open Workflow DSL. Lemline supports basic and
bearer authentication for its HTTP executor. See [Supported Features](lemline-ref-supported-features.html)
for runtime support by protocol and authentication type.

## Policy placement

Define a named policy under `use.authentications` and reference it from the endpoint
with `authentication.use`. Declare referenced secret names under `use.secrets`.

```YAML
document:
  dsl: '1.0.3'
  namespace: examples
  name: bearer-authentication
  version: '1.0.0'
use:
  secrets:
    - apiToken
  authentications:
    partnerAuth:
      bearer:
        token: ${ $secrets.apiToken }
do:
  - getPartnerStock:
      call: http
      with:
        method: get
        endpoint:
          uri: http://127.0.0.1:8787/partner/stock
          authentication:
            use: partnerAuth
```

## Inline basic authentication

Alternatively, configure `authentication.basic` directly on the endpoint. The
`username` and `password` fields supply the credentials.

```YAML
document:
  dsl: '1.0.3'
  namespace: examples
  name: inline-authentication
  version: '1.0.0'
use:
  secrets:
    - tempPassword
do:
  - callServiceWithInlineAuth:
      call: http
      with:
        method: get
        endpoint:
          uri: http://127.0.0.1:8787/partner/stock
          # Define authentication directly here
          authentication:
            basic:
              username: demo
              password: ${ $secrets.tempPassword }
```

## API keys and OAuth 2.0

For a service-specific API key, see [How to Use API Keys](lemline-howto-api-keys.html)
for request headers and query parameters. The [OAuth 2.0 guide](lemline-howto-oauth2.html)
shows the specification's client credentials configuration and describes the runtime limitation.

Use the [Secrets Reference](lemline-ref-secrets.html) to configure secret values outside
the document.

## Run the Examples

Every example on this page is a complete workflow. Complete [the SQLite setup](lemline-tutorial-setup.html), save each example under the file name used below, and run the commands from the setup directory. With the JAR, substitute `java -jar lemline.jar` for `bin/lemline`.

Start the [tutorial shop](lemline-tutorial-order-processing.html#start-the-tutorial-shop) from the root of the Lemline source checkout:

```BASH
docker compose -f examples/tutorial-services/compose.yaml up -d
```

The examples read secrets from the worker's environment. Stop the setup worker with Ctrl+C, export the values, and start it again:

```BASH
export apiToken='demo-token'
export tempPassword='demo-password'
bin/lemline listen --debug
```

Run the next commands from a second terminal in the setup directory.

```BASH
bin/lemline definition post -f bearer-authentication.yaml
bin/lemline instance start examples bearer-authentication
bin/lemline definition post -f inline-authentication.yaml
bin/lemline instance start examples inline-authentication
```

| Example |Expected result |
----------------------------
| `bearer-authentication` |The partner stock with `"authenticatedWith":"bearer"` |
| `inline-authentication` |The partner stock with `"authenticatedWith":"basic"` |

Stop the shop when you are done:

```BASH
docker compose -f examples/tutorial-services/compose.yaml down
```



# Secrets Reference

This page summarizes how Lemline resolves workflow secrets. For a step-by-step guide, see [Managing Secrets in Lemline](lemline-howto-secrets.html).

## Summary

| Aspect |Behavior |
--------------------
| Declaration |`use.secrets`: a list of secret names |
| Source |Runner environment variables with exactly the declared names (no prefix, no case conversion) |
| Access in expressions |`$secrets.<name>` |
| Visibility |Only the names declared by the current workflow |
| Resolution time |On the runner, before each step it executes |
| Storage |`$secrets` is not included in broker messages or persisted workflow state; values copied into task output (including request headers returned by `output: response`) are |
| Missing value |The workflow faults with an `authorization` error (status 403) |
| Child workflows |Resolve their own declared secrets; nothing is inherited from the parent |
| Rotation |Update the variable and restart the runners |

## Declaration

```YAML
document:
  dsl: '1.0.3'
  namespace: examples
  name: declaration
  version: '1.0.0'
use:
  secrets:
    - PARTNER_TOKEN
    - SHOP_CREDENTIALS
do:
  - checkSecrets:
      set:
        tokenSet: ${ $secrets.PARTNER_TOKEN != null }
        user: ${ $secrets.SHOP_CREDENTIALS.username }
```

## Value Types

| Environment value |Value of `$secrets.<name>` |
-------------------------------------------------
| A JSON object, e.g. `{"username":"app","password":"s3cr3t"}` |The parsed object (`$secrets.DB_CREDENTIALS.password`) |
| Anything else |The raw string |

## Where Secrets Can Be Used

`$secrets` is available in every runtime expression of the workflow: HTTP `endpoint`, `headers`, `query`, `body` and authentication policies (`basic`, `bearer`), shell `command` and `arguments`, `if`, `set`, `export`, `output`, and so on.

```YAML
document:
  dsl: '1.0.3'
  namespace: examples
  name: http-secrets-reference
  version: '1.0.0'
use:
  secrets:
    - PARTNER_TOKEN
do:
  - fetch:
      call: http
      with:
        method: get
        endpoint:
          uri: http://127.0.0.1:8787/partner/stock
          authentication:
            bearer:
              token: ${ $secrets.PARTNER_TOKEN }
```

Lemline does not provide its own secret store, file source, or vault integration. Use your platform to inject environment variables (Kubernetes Secrets, Docker secrets mapped to variables, your deployment tool…).

## Missing Secret Error

When a declared secret is not set on the runner, the workflow faults before running the step with:

| Field |Value |
----------------
| `type` |`https://open-workflow-specification.org/spec/1.0.0/errors/authorization` |
| `status` |`403` |
| `title` |`Required secret '<name>' is unavailable` |

This error faults the workflow directly; it cannot be caught by a `try` task.

## Security Notes

* Resolved values are kept in memory only while a step runs.

* An expression that copies a secret into output, context, or a request sends that value onward; Lemline does not mask it.

* With `output: response`, an HTTP task's output includes the headers of the request it sent, including `Authorization`: filter them out (for example with `output.as`) before they become workflow data.

* Every runner that may execute a workflow needs the variables it declares, including runners of other pools that execute its child workflows.

## Run the Examples

Every example on this page is a complete workflow. Complete [the SQLite setup](lemline-tutorial-setup.html), save each example under the file name used below, and run the commands from the setup directory. With the JAR, substitute `java -jar lemline.jar` for `bin/lemline`.

Start the [tutorial shop](lemline-tutorial-order-processing.html#start-the-tutorial-shop) from the root of the Lemline source checkout:

```BASH
docker compose -f examples/tutorial-services/compose.yaml up -d
```

The examples read secrets from the worker's environment. Stop the setup worker with Ctrl+C, export the values, and start it again:

```BASH
export PARTNER_TOKEN='demo-token'
export SHOP_CREDENTIALS='{"username": "demo", "password": "demo-password"}'
bin/lemline listen --debug
```

Run the next commands from a second terminal in the setup directory.

